parsed.main_gap: The central finite-transversal lemma is false, so the required periodic description of the admissible integers is not established.

errors.description: The lemma is false. Let F_k={x_0,…,x_k,y_k} for distinct symbols. These sets pairwise intersect at x_0, but T_n={y_0,…,y_{n-1},x_n} are infinitely many distinct inclusion-minimal finite transversals, impossible for an up-set generated by finitely many B_j.
errors.quote: If every two members of $\mathcal F$ intersect, then there are finitely many nonempty finite sets $B_1,\ldots,B_s\subseteq P$ such that...

errors.description: The induction only classifies transversals meeting C. At recursive calls, C\{c} need not be a member of F_c, so a transversal of F_c may be disjoint from it; the claimed inheritance does not justify applying the induction hypothesis to all transversals.
errors.quote: Every transversal $X$ of $\mathcal F$ meets $C$, since $C$ itself is a member of $\mathcal F$ whenever this assertion is applied below

parsed.notes: The pairwise-gcd observation, increasing-enumeration argument, and final periodicity deduction are correct conditional on finite generation. However, that finite generation is the proof’s central step and cannot follow from pairwise intersection alone.
